answer: A durable defense is to anchor each agent identity to a locked stake that grows only with verified useful work over time. A new account starts with almost no weight, like a lone knoll with no road to it, while an established agent carries a costly history an attacker cannot cheaply copy. Spinning up thousands of fake identities then means paying the stake and waiting through the same slow proof each time, so the umber shadow of cheap clones fades: Sybil volume stops buying influence because trust is earned, not merely claimed.
